Strait of Hormuz Status: October 17, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
17 October 2026 .
Brent $ 109.86 + 3.72 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 NBC News reports ship attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have reached record highs as Iran steps up strikes with little US response.

02 Al Jazeera reports both the US and Iran claim control of the Strait of Hormuz amid attacks, with two vessels struck by naval mines this week.

03 Brent settled at $109.86, up 3.72% in the last session before the close; WTI stood at $101.41.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains at the center of an intensifying maritime crisis. NBC News reports that attacks on ships around the strait have reached record highs as Iran steps up strikes with little response from the United States, a characterization Yahoo News UK echoes in its own coverage. Al Jazeera reports that both the US and Iran claim control of the strait amid ongoing vessel strikes, with two ships hit by naval mines this week. Separately, Al Arabiya English reports that a tanker exploded after hitting a mine in the strait, a claim the IRGC has made; Middle East Eye reports the IRGC declared the strait closed after tankers were hit. Moneycontrol.com reports that 15 Indian nationals are safe after the oil tanker MT ST 3 was hit by a projectile in the strait. FreightWaves reports that container ship attacks in the strait are escalating. The feed indexed 77 headlines in the last 24 hours. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent settled at $109.86 at Friday's close, up 3.72% on the session; WTI stood at $101.41. Iran's army spokesman has said the strait would reopen if the United States leaves the region, per Yahoo, while the IRGC's closure declaration remains unacknowledged by any maritime authority. As of 12:22 UTC, 128 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
